I don't think quantum entanglement can be used directly to make calculation however maybe it can be used to create neural networks. A better use of quantum entanglement is to create a key with a group of qubits at two or more ends of a network that are always changing so to encrypt data transfers.
The rules of Quantum entanglement:
Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon in quantum physics where two or more particles become linked in such a way that the state of one particle cannot be described independently of the state of the others, even if they are separated by a large distance, meaning that measuring one particle instantly reveals information about the other, regardless of the distance between them; this is often described as a "spooky action at a distance" due to its seemingly paradoxical nature. 
Key points about quantum entanglement:
Interconnected particles:
When particles are entangled, they share a single quantum state, meaning their properties are intertwined and cannot be considered individually. 
Instantaneous correlation:
If you measure a property of one entangled particle, you instantly know the corresponding property of the other particle, even if they are far apart. 
No information transfer:
While the measurement results are correlated, no actual information can be transmitted faster than the speed of light.
